title: Say It Again, Slowly
intro: Children keep conversations going by asking adults to repeat sounds and slow them down. Today we add 3 practical listening-repair words so you can stay in a Kannada conversation instead of switching immediately to English.

words.babyAnalogy: Making a small circle with one finger to ask for the song or game again.
words.actionTag: When you miss what a colleague or shopkeeper said, make a gentle repeat gesture and say 'Matte'.

words.babyAnalogy: Moving a flat hand forward very slowly like a crawling turtle.
words.actionTag: When someone speaks Kannada too quickly, move your hand slowly and say 'Nidhaanavaagi'.

words.babyAnalogy: Cupping a hand behind the ear to invite someone to use their words.
words.actionTag: Ask a colleague to tell you a Kannada word or repeat a direction by saying 'Heli' politely.

combos.context: Combining Matte + Heli from Lesson 7 when you miss a phrase.
Combining Illa (Lesson 1) + Matte Heli (Lesson 7) when asked if you understood.

quiz.scenario: A shopkeeper gives you the price in Kannada, but you do not catch it the first time.
quiz.question: How do you politely ask them to repeat it?
quiz.explanation: Matte (Again) + Heli (Say politely) = Say it again, please.

quiz.scenario: Your auto driver is explaining something in Kannada much too quickly for you.
quiz.question: What longer phrase asks them to speak a little slowly?
quiz.explanation: Swalpa (A little, Lesson 4) + Nidhaanavaagi (Slowly) + Heli (Say politely) = Please speak a little slowly.

quiz.scenario: You enjoyed one idli and want the server to bring one more.
quiz.question: What phrase do you use while raising one finger?
quiz.explanation: Matte (One more) + Ondu (One, Lesson 5) + Kodi (Give politely, Lesson 4) = Give me one more, please.
